about: Every setting of config.toml and every variable of .env. The collector checks config.toml against it, the page takes its lists and its own defaults from it (through the copy tools/settings-schema.js writes into web/js/settings.js), and docs/configuration.md carries a reference made from it by the same tool. docs/configuration.md describes the fields.

conditions.name: Under attack
conditions.help: Bans by fail2ban: one in a watched jail, or many of any kind, within a window.

conditions.name: WAN down
conditions.help: The internet checks fail several times in a row.

conditions.name: Unwell
conditions.help: A container is unhealthy, restarting or exited with an error for a while.

conditions.name: Disk full
conditions.help: A configured disk is fuller than its threshold.

conditions.name: Backup overdue
conditions.help: The last completed backup is too long ago.

conditions.name: Pi silent
conditions.help: The Pi of [sources.pi] has not answered for a while.

conditions.name: Device down
conditions.help: A device that alerts is down. It plays in whichever quiet scene is showing.

conditions.name: Running hot
conditions.help: CPU use, averaged over a window, is at or above a threshold.

conditions.name: Memory tight
conditions.help: Available memory, averaged over a window, is at or below a threshold. It plays in whichever quiet scene is showing.

conditions.name: At court
conditions.help: Someone has an SSH session open.

conditions.name: Updating
conditions.help: A configured lock holder, such as nightly maintenance, is running.

tables.help: How the collector runs. The whole table may be left out to take the defaults.

settings.help: Seconds between polls. The displays treat a state file older than three polls as stale and say so.
Folder state.json is written to. compose.yaml mounts KNIGHTWATCHER_OUT here.
Folder for memory.json and the collector's lock. compose.yaml mounts KNIGHTWATCHER_VAR here.

settings.form: an IANA time zone, such as "Europe/London"
settings.help: Zone for the night hours and the times shown in words.
Timeout for each network call. Must be shorter than the time between polls, so a poll every 5 seconds needs it lowered. A device's check uses at most 3 seconds of it for each step.
Pause after a 401, 403 or 429 before the service is called again. Cannot be set below 1200.
Where the host's /proc is mounted, for CPU, memory, load and the lock table.

settings.form: a folder, relative to the one config.toml is in, or absolute
settings.help: The folder of provider files of your own, one provider each, each named after its id with .toml (myflix.toml). Relative, it is taken from the folder config.toml is in, so the default is /etc/knightwatcher/providers in the containers, where compose.yaml mounts KNIGHTWATCHER_PROVIDERS. A folder that does not exist holds none. Read at start and again whenever a file in it changes.

tables.help: When each condition is raised. The whole table, and each condition's own table, may be left out to take the defaults.

settings.help: Conditions, highest first. One left out is never raised. Device down (device_down) must stay in the list while any device alerts.
How long a cause must be absent before its condition clears.

tables.help: Under attack: a ban in a watched jail, or enough bans of any kind, within the window.

settings.help: The window for recent bans.
A ban in one of these jails within the window is an attack.
So is this many bans of any kind within the window.

tables.help: WAN down: the internet checks fail several times in a row.

settings.help: Failed internet checks in a row before the WAN counts as down. Each check is a fresh read of the internet source, so they are as far apart as it is read.

tables.help: Unwell: a container is unhealthy, restarting or exited with an error for a while.

settings.help: How long a container must be unhealthy, restarting or exited non-zero.

tables.help: Disk full: a configured disk is fuller than the threshold.

settings.help: Percent used, on any configured disk, judged on the latest reading.

tables.help: Backup overdue: the last completed backup is too long ago.

settings.help: Hours since the last completed backup.

tables.help: Pi silent: the Pi of [sources.pi] has not answered for a while.

settings.help: How long the second machine must be unreachable.

tables.help: A device down. It has no settings here: each device carries its own pace, its own silence and whether it alerts. An empty table is accepted.
Running hot: CPU use, averaged over the window, is at or above the threshold.

settings.help: CPU use, percent of all cores, averaged over the window: at or above.
The window the CPU is averaged over.

tables.help: Memory tight: available memory, averaged over the window, is at or below the threshold.

settings.help: Memory available, as a percent of all memory, averaged over the window: at or below.
The window available memory is averaged over.

tables.help: At court: someone has an SSH session open.

settings.help: Open SSH sessions needed.
How long a new SSH session keeps the condition up. 0 keeps it up for as long as the sessions it needs are open.

tables.help: Updating. It has no settings: it is active while any configured lock holder is running. An empty table is accepted.
Now showing: a stream is playing.

settings.help: Streams playing needed.

tables.help: Night watch: the quiet hours, in the collector's timezone.

settings.help: Start of the quiet hours, in the collector's timezone. The hours may cross midnight.
End of the quiet hours.

tables.help: CPU, memory and load from the host's /proc, and the size of each configured disk.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read. Should be at least as often as the shorter averaging window; when it is read less often, an average reaches back to the previous read instead.

settings.form: tables of mount and path, such as { mount = "/data", path = "/host/disks/data" }
settings.help: Disks to report. mount is the label written to the file; path is any path inside the container on that filesystem.

tables.help: Container health, from a read-only Docker API proxy.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
Base URL of a read-only Docker API proxy, such as http://192.0.2.10:2375.
Container names to leave out. Use it for one-off and intentionally stopped containers.

tables.help: Whether the internet answers.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.

settings.form: one or more http:// or https:// addresses
settings.help: Tried in turn; the internet is up if any answers with a 2xx. An address avoids depending on DNS.

tables.help: Whether the DNS server answers.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
DNS server to ask.
Its port.
Name to look up. An answer of no error or of "no such name" counts as up.

tables.help: The last completed backup, from the backup log.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
The backup log, inside the container. compose.yaml mounts KNIGHTWATCHER_BACKUP_LOG here.

settings.form: a regular expression with one group
settings.help: Regular expression for a completion line; its first group is the date, in ISO 8601 or the form date prints, such as Thu 15 Jan 03:12:00 UTC 2026.
Zone for a date printed without one.
How much of the end of the log to read.

tables.help: The older way to watch a second machine, kept with no end date: it becomes the first device, named Pi, with the rules it has always had.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
Address of the second machine, such as 192.0.2.4.

settings.form: one or more TCP port numbers
settings.help: TCP ports to try, all at once. A refused connection counts as an answer.

tables.help: Whether a lock holder, such as nightly maintenance, is running.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.

settings.required_problem: list at least one lock holder
settings.form: tables of name and pattern, such as { name = "nightly maintenance", pattern = 'nightly-maintenance\.sh' }
settings.help: While a process whose command line matches pattern holds any lock, name is reported as running.

tables.help: Open SSH sessions.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
The SSH server's port.
Address ranges whose sessions are not counted.

tables.help: Streams playing, from the service its provider reads: Tautulli by default, or Plex Media Server.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
The provider the streams are read through, by its id: the service it reads, and the credentials it reads from .env. A provider of another kind, or one that does not exist, is refused by name.
Base URL of the service the provider reads.

Whether the certificate of an https url is checked. false reads a service whose certificate is self-signed, as a Pi-hole's often is: the connection is still encrypted, but nothing proves it reaches the service named. Only with an https url.

What of the streams leaves the collector, for a display guests can see: names, who is watching and what; titles, what alone; count, how many and nothing else. A name or title held back is never written to the state file.

The name its credentials are read under in .env: KNIGHTWATCHER_<SECRET>_<FIELD>, in capitals, for each field its provider names (Tautulli's is API_KEY, Plex's TOKEN). Left out, it is the provider's id. Set in config.toml alone.

tables.help: Blocked adverts, from the service its provider reads: AdGuard Home by default, Pi-hole 6, or Technitium DNS Server 15 or later.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
The provider the blocked queries are read through, by its id: the service it reads, and the credentials it reads from .env. A provider of another kind, or one that does not exist, is refused by name.
Base URL of the service the provider reads.

Whether the certificate of an https url is checked. false reads a service whose certificate is self-signed, as a Pi-hole's often is: the connection is still encrypted, but nothing proves it reaches the service named. Only with an https url.

The name its credentials are read under in .env: KNIGHTWATCHER_<SECRET>_<FIELD>, in capitals, for each field its provider names (AdGuard Home's are USERNAME and PASSWORD, Pi-hole's PASSWORD, Technitium's TOKEN). Left out, it is the provider's id. Set in config.toml alone.

Average seconds between flies while blocking runs at the household's normal rate, which the service's own statistics give. A burst brings flies faster, at most eight to an event. 0 sends one fly for every blocked query.

tables.help: Bans, and the attack they may add up to, from the provider its from names: fail2ban's own database by default.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.

The provider the bans are read through, by its id: fail2ban, fail2ban's own database at database, which needs its folder mounted and a read grant on the host (docs/configuration.md, fail2ban's database), or a provider file of your own. A provider of another kind, or one that does not exist, is refused by name. Set in config.toml alone, with the mount.
Base URL of the service a provider file of your own reads, and required by one. Refused with fail2ban, which reads database instead. Set in config.toml alone, with from.

Whether the certificate of an https url is checked. false reads a service whose certificate is self-signed, as a Pi-hole's often is: the connection is still encrypted, but nothing proves it reaches the service named. Only with an https url. Refused with fail2ban, which reads no address. Set in config.toml alone, with from.

settings.form: a path inside the collector's container
settings.help: fail2ban's database, as the collector's container sees it through the mount of fail2ban's folder. Read by fail2ban alone, and refused with any other provider. Set in config.toml alone, with the mount.

The name its credentials are read under in .env: KNIGHTWATCHER_<SECRET>_<FIELD>, in capitals, for each field its provider names. fail2ban needs none; a provider file of your own may. Left out, it is the provider's id. Set in config.toml alone.

tables.help: Episodes imported, from Sonarr.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
Base URL of Sonarr.

Whether the certificate of an https url is checked. false reads a service whose certificate is self-signed, as a Pi-hole's often is: the connection is still encrypted, but nothing proves it reaches the service named. Only with an https url.
The name its API key is read under in .env: KNIGHTWATCHER_<SECRET>_API_KEY, in capitals. Left out, it is the provider's id, the section's own name. Set in config.toml alone.

tables.help: Films imported, from Radarr.

settings.help: Whether the source is read. Off (false in config.toml) keeps its other settings for when it is turned on again.
How often the source is read.
Base URL of Radarr.

Whether the certificate of an https url is checked. false reads a service whose certificate is self-signed, as a Pi-hole's often is: the connection is still encrypted, but nothing proves it reaches the service named. Only with an https url.
The name its API key is read under in .env: KNIGHTWATCHER_<SECRET>_API_KEY, in capitals. Left out, it is the provider's id, the section's own name. Set in config.toml alone.

tables.help: Machines on the network to watch, each a [[device]] table at the top level of config.toml. There can be 32, the Pi of [sources.pi] included. A device has exactly one check: an address with one or more ports (host with port or ports), or a web address (url).

settings.form: 1 to 20 printable ASCII characters, with no space at either end
settings.help: What the display calls it. Unique among the devices, ignoring case.
Chooses the headline's word, and the prop the page draws.
Address or name to connect to. Required with port or ports.
One TCP port.
TCP ports tried at the same time; any one answering is enough.
Any HTTP status counts as an answer. No user name or password in it.
Whether a refused connection counts as an answer. Only with host.
Whether the certificate is checked. Only with an https url.
Seconds between checks.
Seconds of silence before the device counts as down.
Whether the device raises Device down (device_down) while it is down.
Whether the device is checked. Off (false in config.toml) keeps it in the list, stops its checks and leaves it off the displays.

tables.help: The world, and the parts it sets: the knight, the monarch at court, the cast, the devices and the words, for every display. A choice made on a wall's settings screen or the admin page is saved over this table, for the whole deployment. The short names of the colours, tones, hair styles and gear are those of the base pack; another loaded pack's are given by long name. A long name, "<pack>/<id>", is checked here only for its form; a display that has not loaded it uses the next level down.

settings.help: The world the display shows, which sets every part below at once: medieval, the world the page ships with, or a world of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<world>". A part set beside the world in this table, or chosen on a display, is kept over the world's; a display that chooses a world takes it whole, over the parts this table sets.

The knight's build, by the base pack's names: Classic (a), the present knight, Broad (b) and Slim (c), or a body of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<build>". The page's own is the base pack's default build, and only a build the packs in use declare is shown.

What the knight carries: the greatsword, the longsword or the crossbow in both hands, or the arming sword (sword_and_shield) or the flanged mace (mace_and_shield) in one hand with the shield in the other. The crossbow is shot where the others are swung.
The knight's skin tone, or a skin swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>".
The knight's hair colour, or a hair swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>".
The knight's hair.

The tabard's colour, which the shields' fields, the coat under the breastplate, the gambeson, the padded sleeves and the short cape take too; or a tabard swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>".
The plume's colour, which the long cloak takes too; or a plume swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>".
The shield carried with a one-handed weapon: the heater shield of the watch, a round shield or a kite shield. With a two-handed weapon no shield is carried.
The helmet: the open helm, a kettle hat, a mail coif or a bascinet. The mail coif carries no plume.
The plume on the helmet: the crest, a tall feather or horsehair. None is drawn on the mail coif.
What the knight wears on the body: the tabard of the watch, a breastplate (cuirass) or a quilted gambeson.
The shoulders: plate pauldrons, layered spaulders (lames) or leather pauldrons.
The arms: plate, mail sleeves or padded sleeves.
The hands: plate gauntlets, leather gloves or mail mittens.
The legs: plate greaves, mail chausses or padded hose.
The feet: riding boots (leather), sabatons or turnshoes.
What hangs from the shoulders: nothing, a long cloak in the plume's colour or a short cape in the tabard's.
Which of the three monarchs sits in the court, or a patron of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<patron>".
The monarch's skin tone, or a skin swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>". The page's own is the court's own skin.
The monarch's hair colour, or a hair swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>". Left out, each monarch keeps the hair the court draws them with ("As drawn").
The colour of the monarch's robe, or a tabard swatch of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<swatch>". Left out, each monarch keeps their own robe (A red, B violet, C green).
The pet who catches the flies the knight cannot, indoors and while the knight is busy: the mouser cat, or a pet of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<pet>".

The pet's coat: the mouser cat's calico, white with ginger and black patches, or ginger tabby; or a coat of a loaded pack's pet by its pack and the coat's id, "<pack>/<coat>", which counts only while that pet is in use. A coat the pet in use does not have gives its first.
Who comes for the knight when an address is banned: the goblin, or a foe of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<foe>".
What a blocked advert turns into: the fly, or a critter of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<critter>".
The drawings of the devices, every kind at once: medieval, or a prop set of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<prop set>". A kind the set does not draw takes the medieval drawing.
The colours and the font of the words over the scene: medieval, or an overlay of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<overlay>".
The words of the quiet line and the captions: medieval, or a word set of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<word set>".
Any slot's item named directly by its long name, "<pack>/<item>", over the key above that chooses the item for that slot: in config.toml a table [look.items], such as main = "kw.base/main.arming".

The drawing of one kind of device, over props for that kind: in config.toml a table [look.devices] whose keys are the kinds, each medieval or a prop set of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<prop set>".

tables.help: How every display shows the words. A choice made on a wall's settings screen or the admin page is saved over this table, for the whole deployment.

settings.help: The size of the headline.
Whether the clock shows 24 hours or 12.
Whether the helmet stays on in the house and the smithy.

tables.help: The scenes that take turns while all is quiet, for every display. A choice made on a wall's settings screen or the admin page is saved over this table, for the whole deployment.

settings.form: one or more quiet scenes, each once
settings.help: The quiet scenes, in the order they take turns: the four the page ships with, or quiet scenes of a loaded pack by their long names, "<pack>/<scene>".
How long each quiet scene shows. The demo shows each for a minute while nothing sets it.

tables.help: Where the knight acts out each condition that more than one scene can play, for every display. A condition left out plays in its own scene. In config.toml each key is a condition and each value a scene, by its short name or a scene of a loaded pack by its long name, "<pack>/<scene>"; a scene that cannot act its condition is ignored, and the condition plays in its own.

settings.help: Where the knight acts out an attack.
Where the knight acts out a full disk.
Where the knight acts out an overdue backup.
Where the knight acts out a silent Pi.
Where the knight acts out a hot CPU.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_OUT
env.help: The host folder the collector writes state.json to. Mounted at /out in both containers, read-only in the server's, which serves it as data/: state.json, and the packs placed in its packs/ folder, which the page reads. Must exist and be writable by the collector's account.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_BACKUP_LOG
env.help: The host's backup log, a single file. Mounted read-only at /host/backup.log.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_DATA_DISK
env.help: Any folder on the data volume, so the collector can see the volume's size. Mounted read-only at /host/disks/data. An empty folder shares nothing but the size.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_VAR
env.help: The host folder for the collector's memory between restarts. Mounted at /var/lib/knightwatcher. Must exist and be writable by the collector's account.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_PROVIDERS
env.help: The host folder of provider files of your own, for services no built-in provider reads. Mounted read-only at /etc/knightwatcher/providers in both containers: the collector reads the files, and the server checks a change on the admin page by them. Must exist and be readable by uid 10001; the repository's own providers folder, empty, is the default.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_SERVER_VAR
env.help: The host folder for the bundled server's own files: the settings saved for every display, in settings.json, and those set on the admin page, in admin.json, with the admin page's sessions. Mounted at /var/lib/knightwatcher-server, the one place the server writes, and read-only at the same place in the collector, which takes up admin.json. Must exist and be writable by the server's account.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_SERVER_ADDRESS
env.form: an address of this host, or empty for all of them
env.help: The host address the bundled server is published on. Left empty, it is all of the host's addresses, IPv4 and IPv6. 127.0.0.1 keeps it to this machine, for a reverse proxy or a monitor on the host; one of the host's own addresses keeps it to that network.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_SERVER_PORT
env.form: a TCP port number from 1 to 65535
env.help: The host port the bundled server is published on. The server listens on 8080 inside its container whatever this is.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.form: a password of at least 12 characters, or empty to leave the admin page off
env.help: The password of the admin page, which changes what the collector watches. Passed to the server alone, never shown, logged or written anywhere else. Left empty, or shorter than 12 characters, the admin page stays off and says why; the walls work as before. A change needs the containers made again, which signs every browser out.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_TAUTULLI_API_KEY
env.help: Tautulli's API key, for the tautulli provider, which [sources.streams] reads by default. In Tautulli: Settings, Web Interface, API, with Enable API ticked.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_PLEX_TOKEN
env.help: The Plex token of the server's owner, for the plex provider, which [sources.streams] reads with from = "plex". Plex lists every stream to its owner alone. In Plex Web, signed in as the owner: any library item's menu, Get Info, View XML; the X-Plex-Token at the end of the address it opens. It is sent in the X-Plex-Token header, never in the address. A Plex token reaches the owner's whole account: keep it as you would the password.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_ADGUARD_USERNAME
env.help: The user name of an AdGuard Home login, for the adguard provider, which [sources.adblock] reads by default. AdGuard Home has no API keys: the collector signs in as a user of its web interface.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_ADGUARD_PASSWORD
env.help: That login's password. AdGuard Home locks an address out for 15 minutes after five bad logins.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_PIHOLE_PASSWORD
env.help: A Pi-hole 6 app password, for the pihole provider, which [sources.adblock] reads with from = "pihole". In Pi-hole: Settings, Web interface / API, Configure app password. The web password works too, but not with two-factor authentication on, since the collector cannot give a code. Version 5 is not supported.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_TECHNITIUM_TOKEN
env.help: A Technitium DNS Server API token, for the technitium provider, which [sources.adblock] reads with from = "technitium". In Technitium, signed in as a user of its own in no group but Everyone, which can view but change nothing: the user menu, Create API Token. The token does not expire. It is sent in the Authorization header, which needs Technitium 15 or later.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_SONARR_API_KEY
env.help: Sonarr's API key, for the sonarr provider, which [sources.sonarr] reads. In Sonarr: Settings, General, Security, API Key.

env.name: KNIGHTWATCHER_RADARR_API_KEY
env.help: Radarr's API key, for the radarr provider, which [sources.radarr] reads. In Radarr: Settings, General, Security, API Key.
